content: Expanding the latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) strategy to include broader populations at the national or local level could significantly enhance its impact. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with sufficient statistical power are urgently required to update recommendations for preventive treatment in contacts of individuals with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). These trials should encompass both adult and pediatric populations, as well as high-risk groups such as people living with HIV. The composition, dosage, and duration of preventive treatment regimens for MDR-TB must be optimized. Additionally, the potential role of newer drugs with strong sterilizing properties should be thoroughly investigated. The effectiveness and safety of preventive treatment for contacts of MDR-TB patients should be evaluated under real-world operational conditions. Further evidence on the risk of progression to active TB among contacts of MDR-TB patients is essential to better understand the benefits of preventive treatment. Epidemiological research should be conducted to assess the burden of LTBI across various geographic settings and risk groups. This data will serve as a foundation for designing tailored interventions at national and local levels, including integrated community-based approaches. Research is also needed to develop service delivery models that ensure proper patient management, including additional interventions for tobacco smokers, illicit drug users, and individuals with harmful alcohol use. Household-based implementation models could improve the efficiency and effectiveness of delivering interventions. Tools should be developed and evaluated to facilitate the monitoring and evaluation of programmatic management of LTBI.
